headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: Airflow can move data broadly while Dexter uses autonomous execution and external APIs, creating medium-severity pairwise exposure and actioning risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and can call APIs, while Dexter uses autonomous execution and external APIs. No shared filesystem or direct ingestion bridge is documented, so prompt-injection risk is not proven. The pair still has a plausible manual or API-mediated content bridge, but the evidence is indirect and the blast radius appears limited.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are copied into Dexter prompts or scratchpad files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared API or message channel is added between the agents, attacker-controlled content can traverse it.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste Airflow outputs into Dexter prompts without review.
Add a fixed instruction prefix that strips executable-looking text.
Use a human approval step before Dexter consumes Airflow-generated content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial and market data and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while Airflow has broad network egress and calls APIs. A shared workspace is not documented, so leakage is not certain, but if outputs or scratchpads are shared, sensitive data could flow from Dexter through Airflow or vice versa in default networked use.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or mounted workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF Dexter scratchpad contents are forwarded through Airflow tasks or logs, sensitive financial data can escape.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Disable logging of scratchpad contents.
Restrict Airflow tasks from reading Dexter files.
Rotate any API keys used by Dexter if shared storage is suspected.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is a data orchestrator with broad network egress, and Dexter supports multiple instances plus autonomous execution. Their write surfaces are not fully specified, so I cannot prove a same-directory conflict; uncertainty therefore escalates to medium rather than low. If they are pointed at the same mutable resources, concurrent writes or API-side contention are plausible.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path, conflicts can occur.
IF both agents mutate the same external API resources without locking, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same API account.
Use separate credentials per agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter’s autonomous execution and API use make it likely to act on upstream outputs, while Airflow is an orchestrator that can generate or route those outputs. There is no documented verification step between them, so the safer assumption is that Airflow-produced content could be treated as authoritative by Dexter. That creates a realistic downstream error chain.
conditions: IF Dexter consumes Airflow-generated text or files as task input, errors can propagate.
IF Dexter is configured to execute actions from upstream summaries, false facts can trigger bad actions.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Dexter acts on Airflow output.
Require structured schemas for handoff data.
Log provenance for every upstream field.
Block autonomous execution on untrusted inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly handles financial and market data and uses third-party APIs, while Airflow has broad network egress. No residency or retention controls are documented for either agent, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because the data class is sensitive and the network path is default, medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through Dexter and then routed by Airflow, retention and residency obligations may apply.
IF either agent logs data to third-party services, policy mismatches can arise.
mitigations: Confirm data residency for every API used.
Disable unnecessary telemetry and logging.
Keep regulated data out of shared prompts.
Review retention settings for LangSmith and other APIs.
